beats.narr: The Vikings tried a rare fair-catch free kick against the 49ers.
It was from 71 yards. The record is 68.
It fell about a yard short.
The kicker had hit from 68 in the warm-ups.

n261123i.end: Rick's take was retracted from 71 yards. It fell short.
n261123i.title: Greatest kick ever. Minus a yard.
n261123i.claim: The Minnesota Vikings used the NFL's rarely seen fair-catch kick rule to try a 71-yard field goal against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday; it fell about a yard short.
n261123i.why: After a fair catch, a team may try a free kick at goal with the defence 10 yards back and not allowed to block it. The NFL record field goal is 68 yards.
facts: The attempt: 71 yards, about a yard short
The kicker hit from 68 yards in warm-ups
Only 21 fair-catch kicks in the Super Bowl era
It came with 11 seconds left in the half

beats.narr: The US Forest Service has released old files on Bigfoot.
In 1982 plaster casts were made of two tracks in Oregon.
He gave eight reasons the tracks were not Sasquatch.
A later memo called it a hoax and closed the case.

n261123j.end: The case stays closed. The witness was not called.
n261123j.title: Point of order: the case is closed
n261123j.claim: The US Forest Service has added to its public archive files on suspected Bigfoot encounters in Montana and Oregon, including a 1982 report on tracks that were later judged a hoax.
n261123j.why: Plaster casts were made of two tracks in Oregon's Umatilla National Forest, and the biologist listed eight reasons they were not Sasquatch. Science has never confirmed Bigfoot exists.
facts: A 1982 report on tracks in north-east Oregon
Plaster casts were made of two of the tracks
The biologist gave 8 reasons it was not Sasquatch
Verdict: "a very clever attempt" at a hoax
